Court No. - 69

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 8991 of 2023
Applicant :- Om Prakash Yadav

Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Sudhir Mehrotra,Suyash Mehrotra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
1. Heard Sri Sudhir Mehrotra, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ajai Singh, learned A.G.A.-I for the State and perused the record.

2. The anticipatory bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant Om Prakash Yadav, seeking anticipatory bail, in the event of arrest in Case Crime No. 65 of 2015, under sections 218, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B I.P.C. and section 13(1)(D), 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Jagdishpura, District Agra.

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for the State raised preliminary objections which are as follows:- (1) the applicant filed a Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 18022 of 2022 (Om Prakash Yadav Versus State of U.P. and two others) in which the second prayer of the applicant was to pass a mandamus/direction to the respondent no. 2 therein not to arrest the petitioner/applicant in the present case crime number in which till the next date of listing or till submission of the police report under section 173(2) Cr.P.C. whichever was earlier, the respondents were restrained to arrest the petitioner.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 18022 of 2022 (Om Prakash Yadav Versus State of U.P. and two others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counter affidavit was called in the matter.
The said writ petition is pending.

It is submitted that the open ended prayer of the applicant in the writ petition with the direction to not to arrest him in the present case crime number yielded a result that an interim protection was granted to him till the next date of listing or till submission of police report under section 173(2)
Cr.P.C. whichever is earlier but since the said writ petition is pending the applicant can always agitate in the writ court for extension of the said interim order.
(2) This is the second anticipatory bail application.
The first anticipatory bail application although was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 05.12.2022 which was filed after rejection of prayer of anticipatory bail of the applicant on 09.11.2022.

The rejection of the second anticipatory bail application before the Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Prevention of Corruption Act) Meerut was at the stage of investigation only and no charge sheet was filed after which the applicant had filed an anticipatory bail application before this Court but now the present anticipatory bail application titled second anticipatory bail application has been filed after charge sheet has been filed against the applicant,
the cognizance has been taken by the trial court and the applicant has been summoned alongwith other co-accused persons as stated in paragraph 30 of the affidavit in support of the bail application which is now not maintainable since the applicant has not approached the concerned trial court by filing anticipatory bail application and even the prayer in the present second anticipatory bail application is for granting anticipatory bail till conclusion of trial, whereas, in the first anticipatory bail application there was no such prayer made and the prayer therein which was only for grant of anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (Prevention of Corruption Act) Meerut
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is argued that looking to the same the present application is not maintainable.
4. Learned counsel for the State prays for and is granted three weeks' time to file counter affidavit even enumerating the preliminary objections in the same.
Learned counsel for the applicant will have two weeks thereafter for rejoinder affidavit.

5. List on 24.01.2024 for final hearing.
6.

Till the next date of listing, the applicant- Om Prakash Yadav, if arrested shall be released on interim anticipatory bail in the aforesaid case on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/-
with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) the applicant shall make himself available on each and every date fixed in the matter by the court concerned.

(ii) the applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court.

Om Prakash Yadav vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35961535/
2 (iii) the applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport the same shall be deposited by him before the concerned court.
7.

sentences.text: In case, the applicant do not co-operate in the proceedings of the trial, this order shall stand automatically recalled/vacated and the applicant shall be taken into custody, forthwith.
8. Further, in default of any of the conditions, the court concerned is at liberty to pass appropriate orders for enforcing and compelling the same.
9. The court concerned shall not be prejudiced by any observation made by this Court while considering the present anticipatory bail application of the applicant.
